name: Feature Wish
summary: A 39 s unofficial feature concept for a famous app: the viewer's own habit acted out on the real interface, the loss, 'what if <brand> had <feature>?', the feature shown working in the product, two everyday examples, a warm joke turn, and a human sign-off. Frame-locked: every cut, camera path, press, word and hit sits on a measured frame.

idea.name: What if <Brand> had <Feature>?
idea.why: the reference's whole promise is one question about a missing feature in an app everyone uses; the slot is a brand plus a feature that brand really lacks

story.name: The Wish Demo
beats: habit (f0-f79): the habit acted in taps on the real interface
loss (f80-f196): you lose it in the pile
demo (f279-f449): the feature pressed, set, done, and the notification arriving
proof (f450-f552): two everyday examples it brings back
warm_turn (f553-f909): a third example that is a person, slowed, warmed and closed by one handwritten word
sign_off (f910-f1165): the maker's credit on black
story.why: problem, turn, the feature in the product, the warm turn and the human sign-off are the order the reference earns its laugh in; naming the beats lets Ice map any brand's gap onto them

style.name: Interface Ride
style.why: one continuous measured camera rides the brand's own light interface floating in black space; word-by-word kinetic captions, hand-drawn notes pointing at buttons, bracket caption pills, a 3D pointer, and a warm old-TV turn with yellow neon handwriting

camera.how: each track maps the shot's world plane to the frame per frame: m = [a, b, tx, c, d, ty] (x' = a x + b y + tx, y' = c x + d y + ty), measured on the reference by optical flow against the anchor frame (similarity, RANSAC). Apply as CSS matrix(a, c, b, d, tx, ty) on the shot's world layer; chain tracks at shared frames with the inverse matrix; directional blur from the camera speed, then keyed to the sharpness windows below
sharpness_windows: rack focus, Gaussian sigma about 10 px falling to 0
giant words soft (about 8 px) behind the sharp pointer

fx.processing: dry and centred until f511 (the two examples); from f512, on the turn's line, a wide stereo reverb: plate or medium room, decay about 0.8 s, pre-delay about 20 ms, wet about 15 to 20 percent, full stereo width, so the voice opens out as the picture warms
fx.verify: on the processed take: side minus mid about -22 dB (within 4 dB) over f512 to f575 and about -9 dB in the 0.4 s after the last word; f445 to f511 stays under -30 dB

fx.processing: needs a listen: the reference's punchline measures brighter and thinner than every other line (centroid 1307 Hz against 434 to 871, 20 percent of energy under 300 Hz against 29 to 68) and overlaps the whoosh at f794 and the hits at f799 and f810, so it may be a band filter, a breathier delivery or effect bleed. Offer the user both: a band filter (high-pass at 250 to 300 Hz with a gentle 2 to 4 kHz lift) or the take as delivered, and let the ear decide
fx.verify: if filtered: centroid 1100 to 1500 Hz and at most 25 percent of energy under 300 Hz on the line

voice.silence: no voice from f576 to f786 and after f804: the turn and the credit run on music and effects
voice.fx_rule: Processing applies only to the user's own recording (or a licensed voice the user started); no voice is ever generated. Each slot's fx is measured on the reference's separated voice stem (demucs htdemucs) with its word timings.
recording_guide: A quiet room with soft things around (a sofa, curtains, a closet of clothes); no fan, no echoing walls.
A phone or a microphone a hand's width (about 15 to 20 cm) from the mouth, slightly to the side so breaths do not hit it; the same place for every line.
Read each slot's line three times in a row, with a short pause between takes; keep the energy of a friend telling a joke, lighter and slower on the turn's line.
Fit each line to its slot's length: the slot's frames divided by 30 give the seconds (for example f69 to f179 is 3.7 s); a stopwatch on the phone is enough.
Record in WAV or the phone's best voice memo setting; send all takes, Ice picks the best by measurement and the user's ear.
alignment: Get word timings for every take (faster-whisper with word timestamps, ice-arabic references/asr-timing.md; ice-type scripts/align_script_to_asr.py maps the written line to the recognised words).
Pick the take whose length is closest to the slot, then the clearest by the user's ear.
Place the take so its first word starts on the slot's first frame (reference first-word frame in voice.reference_words); never move the picture.

When the take runs longer or shorter than the slot, time-stretch it at most 8 percent with pitch kept; beyond that, ask for another take or let the line breathe into the next silence only where the slot is followed by one.
Apply the slot's fx, then check the slot's verify line; the mix ducks the bed under the voice by the ice-audio profile.

steps: 1. Brand and gap: research the brand (dated) and list features its real product lacks that fit the habit-and-loss problem (something users save, collect or queue and then lose). Pick one a stranger names in one line; check on the brand's help pages that it really does not exist today; record the sources in TRUTH.md.

2. Brand test at stage 01, before any build: write the blind description of the concept; a fresh critic runs the brand test and the competitor swap; when a rival could own the idea, ride the feature on a ritual that only this brand has (run-01 passed only on YouTube's bell beside Subscribe). An interface-only film cannot pass the masked frame test: say so at 01 and log it (lesson from run-01, AGENTS.md rule 14).

3. Swap every element for the brand's own, of similar length (within 20 percent of the slot's word or letter range): the habit verbs, the controls, the saved-place name, the toast, the notification wording, the example items, the turn's medium.
4. Keep the 4 brand colour moments and nothing else in brand colour.
5. Presses on every change (the presses block).
6. Truth: every interface word is the brand's real wording or marked as an imagined concept in TRUTH.md; claims are questions or imagined interface; no invented numbers.
7. The 'Unofficial concept, not affiliated with <Brand>' line goes in the delivery note and the suggested post caption, never inside the film.
8. Keep the frame lock: shot frames, cuts, camera tracks, bars, slot geometry and press frames do not move; only content inside the slots changes.
adaptation.distance: a template the user chose is a look and structure the user chose: exempt from the template-distance and fingerprint checks on the axes it fixes (AGENTS.md rule 2, anti-sameness.md 4a); content, brand, words, media and sound are new every time
